title: Smooth size weights and Mellin inversion
pvg_object: smooth weighting of a logarithmic valuation half-space
ant_object: Mellin transform and contour integral without a 1/s factor
forward_translation: W(n/x) becomes (2 pi i)^-1 integral W-hat(s)x^s n^-s ds.
reverse_translation: A Mellin kernel reconstructs the smooth weight under inversion hypotheses.
preserved_information: multiplicative scaling and analytic separation of coefficients from the cutoff
lost_information: sharp boundary behavior and unsmoothed oscillations
trigger: The sum uses W(n/x) with W smooth and compactly supported.
typical_output: smoothed asymptotic with controllable horizontal contours
error_or_wall: Confusing Mellin with Perron introduces a spurious 1/s and wrong constants.
required_certificate: State transform normalization, support/smoothness, starting line, growth bounds, and crossed poles.
positive_example: The One-Theorem 001 proof uses Mellin inversion with no 1/s factor.
counterexample: The sharp indicator 1_{n<=x} does not have rapid Mellin decay.
anti_overclaim: Smoothing simplifies transfer but does not manufacture cancellation.

title: Sharp cutoffs and Perron or Tauberian transfer
ant_object: Perron kernel x^s/s, Tauberian theorem, or desmoothing problem
forward_translation: A sharp cutoff is represented by Perron-type inversion or approached through a named Tauberian/desmoothing result.
reverse_translation: The Perron kernel corresponds to a hard multiplicative-size boundary, not to a smooth weight.
preserved_information: exact cutoff location and summatory coefficients
lost_information: rapid vertical decay; boundary terms become analytically expensive
trigger: The target sum is sum_{n<=x} a_n without smoothing.
typical_output: sharp summatory asymptotic or a named obstruction to removing smoothing
error_or_wall: A smoothed theorem does not automatically imply the same sharp error term.
required_certificate: Control truncation, boundary contributions, vertical integrals, and coefficient signs if using Tauberian methods.
positive_example: Perron inversion includes x^s/s, unlike the Mellin formula for W(n/x).
counterexample: Copying the smooth double-pole constant into a sharp theorem misses derivatives of 1/s.
anti_overclaim: Sharp-cutoff promotion requires a separate certificate.
